ticker.label: Market prices

market.title: Market ticker
market.desc: A strip of live prices under the header.

recovery.title: Save your recovery key
recovery.body: Your data is encrypted. If you forget your password, this key is the only way back in. Nobody else, not even a family admin, can recover it for you.
recovery.bodyChild: Your data is encrypted. If you forget your password, this key gets you back in, or a parent can reset it for you.
recovery.where: Write it down or keep it in a password manager, somewhere other than this device.
recovery.clipboardNote: The clipboard is cleared after a minute.
recovery.confirm: I've saved my recovery key somewhere safe
recovery.recoverDesc: Enter the recovery key you saved when you set up this profile, then choose a new password.
recovery.childHint: No recovery key? A parent can reset your password from the Family page.
recovery.adultHint: No recovery key? An admin can only erase this profile and start it over; the data can't be recovered without your password or key.

history.title: History
history.keep: Every change you make is recorded in your encrypted data. Deleted items can be restored for 30 days; changes stay in history for 90 days.
history.emptyTrash: Nothing deleted in the last 30 days.
history.blocked: Can't undo: this item was changed again later. Undo the later change first.

project.settle: Recorded a split in Lend & borrow

check.intactBody_one: {{count}} change checked since {{date}}. Nothing was altered or removed, and nothing was changed outside Vaulty.
check.intactBody_other: {{count}} changes checked since {{date}}. Nothing was altered or removed, and nothing was changed outside Vaulty.
check.brokenBody: Change {{id}}: {{reason}}. Someone may have edited Vaulty's data directly. Restore a safety copy from Settings if you didn't expect this.

check.outsideBody_other: {{count}} items were changed without going through Vaulty, so they have no history entry.

check.unchained_other: {{count}} older changes from before fingerprints were added aren't covered.

snapshots.title: Safety copies
snapshots.desc: Encrypted copies of your data on this device: one a day, and one before every import, update and restore.
snapshots.empty: No copies yet. One is made when you sign in each day.
snapshots.confirmBody: Your data goes back to how it was on {{date}}. Your current data is saved as a copy first, so you can switch back.
snapshots.note: These protect against mistakes, not against losing this device. For that, export a backup and keep it somewhere else.
snapshots.keep: Up to 7 daily and 4 weekly copies are kept.

members.intro: Everyone gets a separate, private profile with their own password. Admins manage who's on this device but can't open other members' data: each profile is encrypted with its own key. Parents can reset a child's password without losing the child's data.
members.addDesc: You'll get a one-time setup code to give them. They'll use it to choose their own password.

roleDesc.admin: Can also add and remove members and reset children's passwords. Can't open other adults' data.
roleDesc.child: For kids. Parents can reset their password without losing their data.

members.codeDesc: On the sign-in screen, {{name}} picks their profile, enters this code and chooses a password. It works once and expires in 7 days.

reset.title: Reset {{name}}'s password?
reset.body: You hold a parent's recovery copy of {{name}}'s key, so their data is kept. Their password, two-step verification and biometric unlock are cleared, and you get a new setup code for them.

newcode.title: New setup code for {{name}}?
newcode.body: The old code stops working. This profile hasn't been set up yet, so there's no data to lose.

erase.title: Erase {{name}}'s data and start over?
erase.body: {{name}}'s data is encrypted with their own password and recovery key, and no admin can open it. If they've lost both, the only way forward is to delete everything in their profile and issue a new setup code. This can't be undone. If they still have their recovery key, they should use "Forgot password?" on the sign-in screen instead.

remove.title: Remove {{name}} from Vaulty?
remove.body: This permanently deletes their profile and all of their financial data on this device. Make sure they've exported a backup first.

hint.all: Everything you can see: your shared and public items, plus what others share with you

family.offTitle: Family sharing is off for you

family.noShared: Nothing shared for this month yet.

sharing.desc: Share chosen expenses with your family, and see what they share with you. Nothing is shared until you turn this on.

quick.hint: Type a transaction in plain words

quick.keys: Enter to save · Esc to close

sheet.title: Vaulty recovery sheet
sheet.writeKey: Write your recovery key here, exactly as shown in Vaulty.
sheet.useKey: If you forget your password: open Vaulty, choose your profile, select "Forgot password?" and enter this key. Nobody else can recover your data without it.
sheet.useKeyChild: If you forget your password: open Vaulty, choose your profile, select "Forgot password?" and enter this key. A parent can also reset your password.
sheet.backupHint: Backup password reminder (not the password itself):
sheet.backupNote: Encrypted backups (.vaulty files) can be restored on any computer with Vaulty, or opened with the steps in docs/BACKUP_FORMAT.md.
sheet.keepSafeBody: Store it with your important papers, not next to the computer. Anyone holding this key can open your Vaulty data.

backups.title: Backups and export
backups.desc: Safety copies (below) protect against mistakes on this device. A backup file protects against losing the device: keep one somewhere else.
backups.makeDesc: Everything in your profile, locked with a backup password. Opens on any computer with Vaulty.
backups.restoreDesc: Adds what's in a backup to this profile; nothing here is overwritten.
backups.csvDesc: Every transaction, for Excel or Google Sheets. This file is not protected.
backups.sheetDesc: A page to print and keep with your papers: space for your recovery key, backup password hint and where backups are.
backups.passwordDesc: Choose a password just for this backup (at least 10 characters). Without it the file can't be opened by anyone, including you.
backups.hintNote: The hint is stored unencrypted in the file.
backups.plainWarning: This is an older, unprotected backup. It will still be restored.
backups.restoreNote: A safety copy is taken first, and the restore can be undone from History.
backups.filesLeftOut: Document files were left out (over 60 MB); their details are in the backup.

senior.title: Senior mode

errors.data: Something went wrong reading or saving your data. Nothing was lost; try again, and if it keeps happening, restore a safety copy from Settings.
errors.file: That file couldn’t be read or written. Check it still exists and that Vaulty is allowed to use that folder.
errors.format: That file isn’t in a format Vaulty understands.
errors.csv: That spreadsheet file couldn’t be read. Try saving it again as CSV from your bank’s website or Excel.

hotkeys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
hotkeys.desc: Change any shortcut to keys that suit you. They’re saved with your profile.

actions.panic: Lock at once and hide balances

hotkeys.taken: {{keys}} is already used for “{{action}}”. Change that one first.
hotkeys.hint: Click a shortcut, then press the keys. Esc cancels; Backspace turns it off.

calendar.nothingSoon: Nothing due in the next 30 days.
calendar.payBy: Banks are closed that day: pay by {{date}}
calendar.addDesc: Birthdays, renewals, appointments, or a bank holiday where you live.
calendar.name: Name
calendar.importDesc: An .ics file, such as your bank’s or state’s holiday list, or events from another calendar.
calendar.asHolidays: Bank holidays (due dates on them get a pay-by date)
calendar.imported_one: Added {{count}} event. Ones already in your calendar were skipped.
calendar.imported_other: Added {{count}} events. Ones already in your calendar were skipped.
calendar.exportDesc: Saves bills, card due dates and your events as an .ics file that Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook can open.
calendar.includeAmountsDesc: Off by default: calendars are often synced to online services.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.desc: Notifications for bills, card payments and budgets, so nothing is missed.
reminders.onDesc: Bills a few days before (as set on each), card payments 3 days before, budgets at 80% and 100%, and accounts running low. While Vaulty is open and you’re signed in.
reminders.amountsDesc: Off by default: notifications can appear on a locked screen.

locked.settingDesc: Keeps only your payment dates (no names or amounts) outside your encrypted data, to say "a payment is due today" while your profile is locked. Vaulty needs to be running.
locked.title: A payment is due today
locked.body: {{name}}, open Vaulty to see what’s due.

reminders.blocked: Notifications are turned off for Vaulty in your system settings. Turn them on there to get reminders.

test.title: Reminders are on
test.body: This is how Vaulty will remind you about bills and card payments.

budget.title: {{name}}: {{percent}}% of this month’s budget used
budget.body: Open Vaulty to see your budgets.

low.open: Open Vaulty to see your accounts.

safe.title: Safe to spend
safe.desc: Your bank and cash money, after the bills and card payments due before your next income.
safe.untilMonthEnd: until the end of the month ({{date}})
safe.perDay_one: About {{amount}} a day for the next day.
safe.perDay_other: About {{amount}} a day for the next {{count}} days.
safe.short: Bills and card payments due before your next income are {{amount}} more than you have.

forecast.title: Next 60 days
forecast.desc: Bank and cash, with scheduled bills, income and card payments, and about {{amount}} of everyday spending a day.

reports.otherAccounts_one: {{count}} account in another currency isn’t included.
reports.otherAccounts_other: {{count}} accounts in other currencies aren’t included.
reports.otherCurrencies_one: {{count}} transaction in another currency isn’t counted in these {{currency}} totals.
reports.otherCurrencies_other: {{count}} transactions in other currencies aren’t counted in these {{currency}} totals.
reports.placesDesc: Shops, apps and people you paid, largest first.

labels.title: Vaulty report
labels.otherCurrencies: Transactions in other currencies, not included

people.emptyTitle: Keep track of money between you and others
people.emptyDesc: Lent a friend money, borrowed from family, or paid the whole dinner bill? Add the people and Vaulty keeps count, so nobody has to remember.
people.copied: Copied. Paste it into WhatsApp, a text or an email.
people.reminderText: Hi {{name}}, just a friendly reminder about the {{amount}} from earlier. Thanks!

descs.lent: Money leaves your account; they owe you more.
descs.repaid_me: Money comes into your account; they owe you less.
descs.borrowed: Money comes into your account; you owe them more.
descs.i_repaid: Money leaves your account; you owe them less.

what.label: What happened
what.split: Their share of a bill you paid

people.addDesc: Only you see these; they don’t need Vaulty.
people.name: Name
people.splitDesc: You paid the whole bill. Your share counts as spending; the others’ shares are what they owe you.
people.splitOver: The shares add up to more than the total.

subscriptions.title: Looks like a subscription
subscriptions.desc: Charged at a steady rhythm but not tracked yet. Track one to see it coming and get reminded.

tasks.emptyDesc: Note what needs doing: renew insurance, ask for a refund, compare plans. Link a to-do to a bill and it ticks itself off when you mark the bill paid.
tasks.editDesc: Optionally link it to what it’s about.
tasks.title: What needs doing
tasks.billHint: Ticks itself off when you mark this bill paid.

helpers.title: Family helpers
helpers.desc: If you forget your password and lose your recovery key, any two of three people you trust can get you back in. No one can do it alone.
helpers.howItWorks: Choose three helpers: family members on this device, or printed cards you give to people you trust.
helpers.weak: One helper can’t help any more, so only the other two together can. Choose again to have three.
helpers.broken: Fewer than two helpers can help now, so they can’t get you back in. Choose again.
helpers.offDesc: Your helpers and their cards will no longer be able to get you back in.
helpers.chooseDesc: Any two of them together can get you back in. Family members approve with their own password; a printed card has a code to type in.
helpers.printedCard: A printed card for someone else…
helpers.noFamily: No other adults have a profile on this device yet, so all three are printed cards.
helpers.replaces: Your current helpers and cards stop working once you save.
helpers.cardsDesc: These codes are shown only now. Print each card and give it to its holder, in a sealed envelope if you like.

card.title: Vaulty helper card
card.what: {{owner}} chose you as one of three people who can help them back into Vaulty, the app where they keep their money records, if they ever get locked out.
card.when: Only when {{owner}} asks you to, at their own computer. They choose “Get help from family”, then you type this code. One more helper approves too.
card.check: Make sure it really is {{owner}} asking. If someone else asks for this code, don’t give it.
card.keep: On its own it opens nothing. It stops working if {{owner}} chooses new helpers.

signIn.title: Get help from family
signIn.desc_one: One helper has approved. One more is needed.
signIn.desc_other: Any two of your helpers can let you back in. Ask them to approve here.
signIn.ready: Two helpers approved. Choose a new password, {{name}}.
signIn.twoStepHint: Two-step sign-in stays on. A backup code works too.

notice.title: You helped someone back in
notice.desc: Your approval was used to let a family member back into their profile.
notice.advice: If you don’t remember doing this, tell them and an admin straight away.

nomineeCard.title: Vaulty nominee card
nomineeCard.what: {{owner}} named you their nominee in Vaulty, the app where they keep their money records. If something happens to them, this card lets you see a summary of their accounts, cards, investments and loans, to help the family claim and settle them.
nomineeCard.when: On {{owner}}’s computer, open Vaulty, choose their profile, then “Forgot your password?” and “I’m their nominee”. Type this code to start a waiting period.
nomineeCard.check: After the wait, come back with this card. One of {{owner}}’s helpers approves, and the summary opens. You can print it or save it as a PDF.
nomineeCard.keepTitle: Keep this card with important papers, such as a will.
nomineeCard.keep: On its own it opens nothing. It stops working if {{owner}} chooses new helpers or another nominee.

estate.title: {{name}}’s money: in case of emergency
estate.accountsHint: Contact each bank with a death certificate to claim these; notes often say who the nominee is.
estate.debtsHint: Tell each lender. Some loans carry insurance that pays them off.
estate.cardsHint: Only the last four digits are kept. Ask each issuer to close the card.
estate.regularHint: Bills to keep paying or stop, and income to claim or transfer.
estate.name: Name
estate.footer: From Vaulty. Figures are as the member recorded them; check them with each bank or company.
estate.readOnly: Read-only: nothing can be changed here.
estate.previewNote: This is what your nominee would see.
estate.documentsHint: Policies, IDs and papers, with where each original is kept.
estate.policiesHint: Claim these with the insurer; the nominee and policy number are needed.

nominee.title: Nominee
nominee.desc: Someone who can see a read-only summary of your money if something happens to you, like a bank nominee. They need their card, a waiting period, and one of your helpers.
nominee.dialogDesc: They get a printed card. With it and one of your helpers, after the waiting period, they can see a summary of your accounts, cards, investments, loans and regular payments. Nothing can be changed.
nominee.name: Their name
nominee.waitHint: If you sign in during the wait, you’re told and can cancel it.
nominee.letterPlaceholder: Where papers are kept, who to call, anything else they should know.
nominee.letterHint: Kept encrypted. Only you and, after the wait, your nominee can read it.

signIn.title: {{name}}’s nominee
signIn.start_one: Type the code on your nominee card. {{name}}’s summary opens after {{count}} day, unless they sign in and cancel.
signIn.start_other: Type the code on your nominee card. {{name}}’s summary opens after {{count}} days, unless they sign in and cancel.
signIn.comeBack: Come back then with your card. One of {{name}}’s helpers will need to approve too.
signIn.ready: The waiting period is over. One of {{name}}’s helpers approves, then your card opens the summary.
signIn.askHelper: Ask one of {{name}}’s helpers to approve:
signIn.readOnly: A nominee sees a summary only. Nothing can be changed.

request.title: Your nominee asked to see your summary
request.desc: Someone used your nominee card on {{started}}. Your summary opens to them on {{ready}}.
request.advice: If you didn’t expect this, cancel it, and think about choosing new helpers so the card stops working.

documents.emptyTitle: Your family’s important papers, in one place
documents.emptyDesc: Passports, Aadhaar and PAN, insurance policies, property papers, your will. Keep scans encrypted here, note where the originals are, and get reminded before anything expires.
documents.newDesc: Save the details, then attach scans or photos.
documents.title: Name
documents.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Jane’s passport, Jimmy’s PAN card
documents.keptAtPlaceholder: e.g. Steel almirah, top shelf; bank locker
documents.noFiles: No files yet. Attach a PDF or a photo of each side.
documents.encrypted: Files are encrypted with your profile’s key. PDFs open in your own viewer: save a copy to open one.

device.title: This computer
device.desc: Settings for this computer, for everyone who uses Vaulty on it.
device.trayDesc: Quick add, open Vaulty or lock it from the icon.
device.shortcutDesc: A shortcut that opens quick add while you’re in any app. Locked? You sign in first.
device.keepRunning: Keep running when the window is closed
device.keepRunningDesc: Reminders and the shortcut keep working. Quit from the icon’s menu.
device.keepRunningNeedsTray: Needs the icon, so Vaulty can be opened and quit again.

investments.emptyDesc: Read your mutual fund statement from CAMS or KFintech to bring in every folio and transaction, or add shares, deposits and gold yourself.
investments.xirrHelp: Yearly return, counting when each amount went in and came out
investments.name: Name
investments.dialogDesc: Units, the latest price and what you paid. Vaulty works out the value and gain.
investments.fromStatement: From your fund statement up to {{date}}. Reading a later one updates it.
investments.namePlaceholder: e.g. Example Flexi Cap Fund – Direct Growth
investments.statementDesc: The consolidated account statement (CAS) PDF from CAMS or KFintech, with every fund you hold.
investments.passwordHint: The password you set when you asked for the statement. It's used only to open the file and isn't kept.
investments.stays: The file is read on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.
investments.unbalanced: Units don't add up to the closing balance
investments.unbalancedHelp: Some rows may not have been read. The closing balance from the statement is used, so the value is still right; the transaction list may be short.
investments.fundPricesDesc: Keeps the value of your funds current between statements.
investments.fundPrices: Update fund prices daily from AMFI
investments.fundPricesHelp: Once a day, Vaulty downloads AMFI's public list of every fund's latest NAV and updates the funds you hold. Nothing about you or your funds is sent; no account or key is needed.
investments.noFundsToPrice: There are no funds with an ISIN to price yet.
investments.pricesUpdated_one: {{count}} fund updated to the prices of {{date}}.
investments.pricesUpdated_other: {{count}} funds updated to the prices of {{date}}.
investments.nomineeHint: As registered with the fund house or depository

projects.accountNameHelp: The name your bank or UPI app showed for them. It helps match bank statement rows to this payment.
projects.alsoRecordHelp: Adds the expense to the account it was paid from, tagged with the project's name, so balances stay right.
projects.dialogDesc: A home renovation, a wedding, a trip: anything you want to keep the bills and payments of together.
projects.emptyDesc: Keep every bill, labour charge and payment for a renovation, wedding, trip or business set-up in one place, with totals by section and what's still owed to each person.
projects.itemDesc: One line of a bill: what it was, how many, at what rate.
projects.itemsAdded_one: {{count}} item added. Add the next one.
projects.itemsAdded_other: {{count}} items added. Add the next one.
projects.linkDesc: These payments look like transactions already in Vaulty, such as rows from a bank statement. Linking them avoids counting the money twice.
projects.linkHint_one: {{count}} payment matches a transaction in your accounts.
projects.linkHint_other: {{count}} payments match transactions in your accounts.
projects.name: Name
projects.noAccounts: Add an account in {{currency}} first to record payments as transactions.
projects.noPeople: Add who you bought from or paid, and their balance shows here.
projects.ownColumnsHelp: Add anything else to note per item, named as you like: a part number, colour, warranty, who approved it. Number columns are totalled.
projects.paymentDesc: Money paid out for the project: an advance, an instalment or a full payment.
projects.peopleHelp: Bills and payments are matched by the name of who you bought from or paid.
projects.removeSectionHelp: Removing a section keeps its items and payments, without a section.
projects.sectionsHelp: Parts of the project, to see totals and budgets for each. You can change them later.
projects.willUnlink: The link to the transaction will be removed when you save. The transaction stays.

renovation.label: Home renovation
renovation.name: Home renovation
renovation.sections: Civil work|Electrical work|Plumbing|Carpentry|Painting|Flooring and tiles|Fixtures and fittings

projects.standardColumnsHelp: Untick the ones you don't need, and rename any to suit the project, such as Part instead of Item or Supplier instead of Bought from.
projects.billsHelp: Bills, invoices and receipts. Point each one at the item or payment it's for.
projects.noBills: No bills kept yet. Attach PDFs or photos of bills and receipts.
projects.billsEncrypted: Files are encrypted on this computer and included in encrypted backups.
projects.readDesc: Check each line against the bill and correct anything that was read wrongly. Untick lines you don't want. The bill stays with the project.
projects.noBillTotal: The bill's total wasn't found. These lines come to {{sum}}; check it against the bill.
projects.totalMatches: These lines come to the bill's total of {{total}}.
projects.totalDiffers: These lines come to {{sum}}, but the bill says {{total}}. Look for a line that was missed or read wrongly.
projects.readPhoto: These were read from a photo, so check every number.
projects.membersHelp: Who shares this project's costs, and in what share: 1 each splits equally; 2 pays twice as much as 1. Mark which one is you.
projects.splitEmptyDesc: For a trip with friends or a shared purchase: add who's in it, say who paid each payment, and see who owes whom.
projects.splitBasis: Split of the {{total}} paid so far, by each person's share.
projects.copied: Copied. Paste it into a message.
projects.shareDesc: Saves the whole project in a file locked with a password, to send to someone who uses Vaulty. When they send it back after changes, opening it brings your copy up to date.
projects.sharePasswordHint: At least 8 characters. Tell it to them another way (say it, or a different app), not with the file.
projects.shared: Saved. Send the file, and tell them the password separately. Links to your own transactions aren't in it.
projects.billsLeftOut_one: {{count}} bill was left out to keep the file small.
projects.billsLeftOut_other: {{count}} bills were left out to keep the file small.
projects.openSharedDesc: A .vaultyproject file someone sent you, with the password they told you.
projects.willUpdate: You already have this project as “{{name}}”. Opening the file brings it up to date; your links to your own transactions stay.
projects.whichAreYou: Which one of these is you?
projects.recordDesc: Adds what each person owes you, or you owe them, to Lend & borrow, so it's tracked until it's paid. Recording again later adds only what changed.
projects.nothingToRecord: Everything from this split is already in Lend & borrow.
projects.alreadyRecorded: Already recorded: {{what}}. This adds the change.
projects.spendingCategoryHelp: Your spending there changes to your own share: down when you paid more than your share, up when others paid for you.
projects.improvementHelp: Renovation, an extension, new fittings: what it costs adds to the property's cost when you sell it, which lowers the capital gains tax. Totals are shown by financial year.
projects.improvementNote: Keep these bills: when the property is sold, this cost is added to what it cost you. Check the rules for your sale with a tax adviser.
projects.warrantyHelp: Adds it to Documents, with a reminder before the warranty ends.
projects.warrantyInDocuments: It's in Documents, with a reminder before the warranty ends. Changing the date updates it there.

goals.emptyBody: Set a target and a date, point it at the accounts and investments you're saving in, and see what it takes each month.
goals.projected: On this plan you'd have {{amount}} by the date, growing at {{rate}}% a year.
goals.dialogDesc: How much, by when, and where the money is kept.
goals.name: Name
goals.todaysMoney: This amount is in today's money
goals.todaysMoneyHint: Prices rise: the target grows by inflation until the date.
goals.noSources: No accounts or investments in this currency yet.
goals.shareHint: Count part of an account (say 50% of savings) when it's kept for more than one goal.
goals.rateHint: Roughly: savings account 3–4%, fixed deposit 6–7%, debt funds 7%, equity funds 10–12% over the long run.
goals.projectedLegend: Lighter bar: where this plan gets you by the date

calc.estimate: Estimates: actual returns, rates and taxes vary.

sip.name: SIP
sip.desc: Investing a fixed amount every month, optionally raised each year.

lumpsum.name: Lump sum
lumpsum.desc: One amount invested now and left to grow.

emi.name: Loan EMI
emi.desc: The monthly instalment, total interest, and what paying a little extra each month saves.

fd.name: Fixed deposit
fd.desc: What a deposit grows to, compounded the way banks do.

rd.name: Recurring deposit
rd.desc: A fixed amount deposited every month, compounded quarterly.

ppf.name: PPF
ppf.desc: Public Provident Fund: deposits at the start of each year, up to ₹1.5 lakh, for 15 years or more. The rate is set by the government each quarter.

goal.name: Goal
goal.desc: How much to save each month to reach an amount by a date.

retirement.name: Retirement
retirement.desc: The savings needed to cover today's expenses, as prices rise, from retirement onwards.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.desc: What something costs in a few years as prices rise.
inflation.today_worth: That amount then is worth today

insurance.emptyTitle: Keep your policies in one place
insurance.emptyBody: Life, health, car and home cover with premiums reminded before they're due, who the nominee is, and claims as they progress.
insurance.dialogDesc: What it covers, the premium and when it's due. Attach the policy document in Documents.
insurance.name: Name
insurance.forParents: This covers my parents (a separate tax deduction limit)
insurance.multiple: {{n}}× your income over the last 12 months ({{income}})
insurance.noIncome: No income recorded in the last 12 months to compare with.
insurance.ruleOfThumb: A common rule of thumb is 10–15× yearly income for those who depend on you.
insurance.noNominee: No nominee noted. Check one is registered with the insurer.
insurance.payDesc: Counts towards your tax deductions in the tax planner.
insurance.movesOn: The next due date moves on by one period.
insurance.singleNote: A single premium: nothing more will be due.

networth.title: Net worth
networth.desc: What you have, less what you owe, at the end of each month.
networth.empty: Add accounts or investments to see how your net worth changes.
networth.chartLabel: Net worth by month: what you have above the line, what you owe below, the net as a line
networth.note: Balances start from each account's opening date. Investments use the units and price known on each date; ones typed in without history count at today's value throughout.

nominees.none: Add bank accounts, investments or policies to note who their nominee is.
nominees.allSet: Every account, investment and policy has a nominee noted.
nominees.why: Without a registered nominee, a family may need a succession certificate to claim the money. Note who's registered here, and check it with the bank, fund house or insurer.
nominees.placeholder: Name, and share if more than one

anomalies.title: Worth a look
anomalies.desc: Spending in the last 30 days that stands out. Mark it fine if it's expected.

journal.reviewDue: {{month}} is over. How did it go?
journal.emptyTitle: A place to think about money
journal.emptyBody: Note why you made a decision, what worried you, what went well. Reading it back a year later is the useful part.
journal.reviewDesc: The month's figures are kept with what you write, as they are now.
journal.dialogDesc: Only you can read this; it's kept encrypted with the rest of your data.
journal.refreshFacts: Update the figures to what they are now
journal.prompt: What happened, what you decided and why…
journal.reviewPrompt: What went well, what didn't, what to change next month…
